elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If abdominal aortic aneurysm likely: avoid giving IV fluids even if BP < 90/60 (raising blood pressure may worsen rupture).

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If BP < 90/60 or pancreatitis likely, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 90. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If infection likely, give ceftriaxone2 1g IV and single dose metronidazole3 400mg orally.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If pain severe, give morphine 5-10mg IM, repeat 4-6 hourly until patient referred, or give diluted morphine4 3-10mg slow IV: start with 3mL IV over 3 minutes. If needed, give another 1mL/ minute until pain improved, up to 10mL. Stop if BP < 90/60.

1Common allergens: medication, food or insect bite/sting within past few hours. 2Do not mix Ringer's lactate and IV ceftriaxone. 3Advise no alcohol until 24 hours after last dose. 4Dilute 10mg morphine with 9mL sodium chloride 0.9%.

Dyspepsia (heartburn) likely • Advise to stop NSAIDS (e.g. ibuprofen/aspirin). If smoking, encourage to stop 164. Avoid fizzy drinks, fatty/late night meals. • Limit alcohol/caffeine/spicy food. Eat small frequent meals. Sleep on left side with upper body elevated. • If BMI ≥ 25 and waist circumference ≥ 80cm (woman) or ≥ 94cm (man), gastro-oesophageal reflux disease likely. Assess and manage overweight/obesity 156. • Discuss/refer if any of: Hb < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), blood in vomit or black, sticky, tar-like stool (melaena), difficulty or discomfort/pain with swallowing, persistent vomiting, unintentional weight loss, recurrent symptoms with: > 50 years, history of previous gastric surgery, family history of stomach/ oesophageal cancer. • Give omeprazole 20mg daily for 14 days. Avoid if on atazanavir/ritonavir. Discuss with specialist. • Advise to return if no better after 7 days. Refer.
